newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra eases media rules for foreigners.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra eases media rules for foreigners.

text.p: The Australian government said on Wednesday that foreign investors would have to seek approval for portfolio investments in the media sector only if they wanted to hold five percent or more in the company.
A portfolio investment is an interest where the investor does not have any operational control over the company.
Previously, all foreign investments in the Australian media sector, except those in newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, required government approval.
The five percent threshold previously applied to investments in Fairfax only, the government said in a statement.
"(The previous notification requirements) involved a heavy administrative burden for investors and the Foreign Investment Review Board," the government said.
It said all other aspects of Australia's foreign investment policy in relation to the media sector remained unchanged.
